text:
The strongest anomaly is M5, the tail source. Its Vds of 0.222 V is below its Vdsat of 0.546 V, so it is in triode. The tail node sits at vcm − Vgs(M2) ≈ 0.9 − 0.68 ≈ 0.22 V, which leaves only 0.22 V of headroom for the tail. M5 needs a Vdsat below about 0.2 V. Its current, about 26 µA, is roughly what the mirror should deliver. The problem is its W/L: at W/L ≈ 0.86 the Vdsat is about 0.55 V. In triode the tail no longer regulates the input-pair current, which would explain the large offset sensitivity to the input-pair devices and the shifted output level. The f_unity failure is consistent with R1·Cf being set correctly, since the measured 3.9 MHz is close to the ideal 4.24 MHz with finite-GBW roll-off.

M6 (the bias reference) and M7 (the output-stage device) are the next candidates because they appear in the f_unity sensitivities and set the GBW and output-stage operating point. I did not verify these by re-simulating, so the ranking rests on the operating-point and sensitivity data.

```json
{"ranking": ["M5", "M6", "M7"], "fault": "Tail current source M5 is mis-sized (W/L too small, about 0.86, for the available headroom). Its Vdsat of about 0.55 V exceeds its Vds of 0.22 V, so it operates in triode and no longer sets a clean tail current. This drives the input-pair imbalance and the output offset (about -0.10 V from 0.9 V). Widening M5 or shortening its L should lower Vdsat below about 0.2 V so it saturates."}
```
